thread:
Nina: Heads up — Python quickstart on docs site throws AttributeError for new users. I ran through the steps in README and got: 
```
AttributeError: 'RedwoodClient' object has no attribute 'text_generate'
```
Jorge: Which README command did you use? Link?
Nina: docs.redwood.ai/quickstarts/python-onboard -> the sample instantiates client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')) then calls client.text_generate('hello').
Priya: We removed text_generate in 1.4; new method is client.generate. Looks like docs still have the old alias. Also embeddings example uses client.create_embeddings(...) but SDK now expects client.embeddings.create(...).
Nina: Yep, I patched locally and it fixed the error. Will users notice and rage? :grimacing:
docs-bot: :robot_face: docs-linter detected 3 issues in /quickstarts/python-onboard/README.md: deprecated API usage (text_generate), embeddings callsite mismatch (create_embeddings -> embeddings.create), missing env var example for REDWOOD_API_KEY. See http://ci.internal.redwood/docs-lint/4599
Jorge: Oof. How widespread is this? Any other quickstarts?
Priya: I searched the repo quickly — 6 Python snippets still using text_generate, 2 using create_embeddings. Looks like copy/paste from old samples.
Ken: I can open a single PR to update all Python quickstarts to the current API surface and add a tiny smoke test that runs pytest -q against the example with a local mocked server. That'll catch these mismatches early.
Nina: That sounds ideal. Can we also add a note in the SDK changelog and the docs migration guide? People copy/paste examples directly, so the migration guide should have a small table: text_generate -> generate, create_embeddings -> embeddings.create.
Priya: Agree. I drafted https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/380 to add a migration table; will expand with the exact call signatures.
Ken: PR for quickstarts: https://github.com/redwood-inference/examples/pull/1558 — updates README snippets, fixes env var example to show `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_...`, and adds .github/workflows/quickstart-py-smoke.yml which spins up a tiny mock HTTP server and runs the example.
Jorge: Nice. Can you paste the corrected Python snippet so I can eyeball the style?
Ken: Sure — updated snippet below: 
```python
# index.py (snippet)
import os
from redwood import RedwoodClient

client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY'))

async def main():
    resp = await client.generate(model='redwood-1', prompt='hello')
    print(resp.text)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    import asyncio
    asyncio.run(main())
```
Priya: Tiny nit — use synchronous example too for folks new to asyncio. Add a short sync wrapper snippet.
Nina: Also add a line about retries — SDK default for Python is a 3x exponential backoff, but docs didn't mention it and examples that assume instant success can confuse users when they hit transient 502s.
Ken: Will add a short paragraph in README: "The SDK retries transient errors (3 attempts, exponential backoff). See SDK retries docs for customization."
docs-bot: :white_check_mark: PR 1558 passed docs-lint and smoke CI.
Jorge: Great. Assigning follow-ups: @Priya expand migration guide, @Ken merge examples PR and add smoke CI to quickstarts, @Nina confirm published docs update fixes the community thread.
Nina: On it. I'll respond in community Slack and paste the PR links.
Priya: I'll also open a small issue in the Python SDK repo to add a deprecation warning for text_generate to help out users who have older code.
Ken: Thanks everyone — should cut down on onboarding friction. :party_parrot:
